subject: Fastline discovery — activation readiness, queueing behavior & scale-up targets
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@fastline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fastline discovery — activation readiness, queueing behavior & scale-up targets

Aaron — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we draft the activation test plan.

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Primary SLOs: 99th pctl tail latency <= 250ms for short request paths (single-turn chat embeddings and short completions); end-to-end streaming responsiveness (first-stream token latency) <= 400ms; 95th pctl for streaming token inter-arrival <= 120ms.
- Throughput & concurrency targets: baseline steady throughput ~700 tokens/sec, expected peak bursts up to ~2,800 tokens/sec (4x baseline) for short windows (1–3min). Concurrency expected ~220 active sessions, with 350 concurrent requests during peak marketing events.
- Autoscale behavior desired: scale-up to handle peak burst within 25–35s from baseline; prefer warm pool of prewarmed instances that can cover the first 60s of a burst.
- Queueing policy: customer prefers short queuing (client timeout ~30s). Acceptable fallback behavior: gracefully degrade to a smaller model variant or rate-limit non-essential traffic rather than drop active streams.
- Observability: need token-level latency histograms, per-instance concurrency, queue length, and a health signal for warm pool readiness. Retention for these metrics for at least 90 days for post-mortem.

Proposed Redwood actions (we’ll own deliverables unless noted):
1) Share activation test plan (attached v1) with scenarios that mirror your expected burst shapes and streaming mixes.
2) Run a 2-phase activation run: (A) prewarm & soak for 15m, (B) scripted burst ramp to peak over 90s.
3) Provide a gating checklist that includes scale-up time measurement, 99p latency during burst, and warm-pool coverage fraction.
4) Instrument a short dashboard and a pre-configured alert for queue length > 10 per instance and for tail-latency regression.

Open questions for Fastline:
- Can you confirm the client-side timeout strategy? We heard 30s but want to ensure mobile SDKs won’t aggressively retry and exacerbate the burst.
- Any regulatory constraints on telemetry export (IP redaction, only aggregated metrics)?

Next steps / timeline:
- You: confirm time window for a staged activation (preferred: next Thurs 14 May 2029, 09:00–11:00 PT).
- Us: update the test plan with your answers and schedule a 30-min pre-run sync the day before.

Attachments: activation_test_plan_v1.xlsx (scenarios + measurement sheet), fastline_slo_summary.pdf (our restatement of the SLOs).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm the slot.

—
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@fastline.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fastline discovery — activation readiness, queueing behavior & scale-up targets

Thanks Logan — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Client timeout: 30s is correct for web/mobile. For our server-to-server integrations we have a 60s window and we will toggle retries off for the activation window to avoid thundering herds.
- Telemetry: we can export aggregated metrics; anything with PII (user IDs) will require redaction. 90-day retention is acceptable.
- Warm pool sizing: our ops team prefers prewarmed capacity to cover at least 50% of the anticipated peak; remainder should be recoverable via autoscale within the 25–35s window.

One request: can Redwood surface a per-request fallback tag in logs when a smaller model or degraded path is used? That will help our business logic flag degraded responses for downstream scoring.

We can confirm the 14 May slot, 09:00–11:00 PT. Please send calendar and the final plan.

—
Aaron Lee
Head of Platform, Fastline
aaron.lee@fastline.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fastline discovery — activation readiness, queueing behavior & scale-up targets

Looping in ops/solutions notes so we have a ready test plan for Monday:

Key technical changes I propose to the attached v1 test plan:
- Add a streaming-first scenario: 60% streaming token load (long-lived streams, intermittent tokens) + 40% short completions to validate first-token latency and inter-token pacing.
- Warm pool strategy: recommend a hybrid warm pool of 12 prewarmed endpoints (sized to Fastline traffic mix) with auto-eviction policy after 20m idle; combine with fast cold-start path using compiled kernels we pre-select for their model family.
- Queueing policy implementation: implement a two-tier queue. Tier A (1–30s) will try to service with existing idle prewarmed endpoints. Tier B (30–60s) will allow controlled batching with degraded model fallback if warm pool coverage < 40%. We'll surface a fallback header (x-rw-degraded: true) for logs as Aaron requested.
- Measurement harness: we will capture per-request traces including model variant, warm_pool_hit (true/false), queue_ttl, and kernel_path. These will be anonymized to avoid PII leakage.

Proposed acceptance criteria for the run:
- Scale-up time (baseline->peak covered capacity) <= 35s in 90% of runs.
- 99p tail latency during burst <= 350ms for short completions; first-token latency <= 450ms for streams.
- Warm-pool coverage fraction >= 50% of initial burst tokens.

I attached a patched activation_test_plan_v1.xlsx (will upload updated sheet to the Drive link). Ben — can you validate the resource sizing for 12 endpoints with our quant profile? Monica — please confirm observability dashboard template and alert thresholds.

I'll draft a 30-min pre-run agenda once Logan confirms the calendar.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
